Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., April 30, 1920 Mr. Sam Kami Cashmere, Washington Dear Sir: There is enclosed herewith your post-office money order which you sent to Joseph Atkins. A short time ago, Joseph enlisted in the United States Army at Camp Lewis, Washington, 35th Infantry, Company F, but is at present with the regiment at Butte, Montana. It is presumed that these troops will return to Camp Lewis within a short time. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. :MG Enc. P. O. M. O. 100109 $15.00. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., March 16, 1920 Fred C. Morgan, Supt Colville Indian Agency Naspelem, Washington Sir: There is enclosed herewith Official Receipt No. 176186 covering transfer of $25.00 to the credit of Joseph Atkins at this office. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. :MG Enc. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Indian Agency, Nespelem, Wash., March 12, 1920. Mr C V Peel, Special Agent, Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Mr. Peel: For credit to the account of Joseph Atkins enclosed, payable to your order, please find check #5488 in the sum of $25.00. Very truly yours, Fred C Morgan Superintendent. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent must show to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided for. All blank spaces be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. Applicable laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. Compliance must be given to all orders and instructions promulgated in connection with the new course of study issued December 1, 1915. The information as to public school facilities called for in the certificate of the Superintendent (third page hereof) must be given, and all superintendents are especially directed to exhaust every means to secure enrollment of Indian children in the State public schools, pursuant to instructions heretofore issued in this regard. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Indian Agency, Nespelem, Wash., Dec. 24, 1919. Supt. E. H. Hammond, Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Mr. Hammond: In a letter dated December 8th Joseph Atkins informs me that he would like to have about $50.00 of his money with which to purchase clothing. For expenditure under your supervision I am enclosing check #4711 for $50.00, payable to you and drawn against his bank account. Very truly yours, [signature] Superintendent. SJ-Encl. cc to JA. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Omak, Washington, Oct. 23, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt., Cushman, Washington. Dear Sir:- Joseph Atkins has just notified me that he has not yet received a ticket from you to come to school. I have your letter saying his application had been approved by Mr. Morgan and I am writing him today to inform him that I have requested to have ticket placed for him at Cashmere at once. Very respectfully, W A Galbert Farmer. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Oct. 20, 1919 Mr. W. A. Talbert Omak, Washington My dear Mr. Talbert: Mr. Morgan has approved the application of Joseph Atkins of Cashmere. Please advise this young man to report immediately. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG UNITED STATES RAILROAD ADMINISTRATION W. G. McADOO, DIRECTOR GENERAL OF RAILROADS CONSOLIDATED TICKET OFFICES Tacoma, Wash., Nov. 6, 1919. Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt., Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear Sir:- I am returning your voucher for $5.76 covering ticket furnished Joseph Atkins from Cashmere, Wash., to Tacoma, which I have signed as requested, for which please send me your check.
